question: 1(a)
exact_skill: Trace the actual unsafe copies and construct a conditional control-flow payload
question_paraphrase: For the printed 32-bit little-endian C program, decide whether hack() can be invoked and give symbolic-address payload pseudocode. All defenses are disabled; main reads 300 bytes into str[30]; overflow_in_action has buffer[300], two heap pointers, strcpy calls and an indirect callback.
coverage_note: The source does not fix frame offsets or heap allocator layout. A conditional symbolic payload is justified; an unconditional offset is not.

question: 1(c)
exact_skill: Untrusted key bundled with its own signature; attacker positions
question_paraphrase: ARTBot broadcasts to learn CSBot’s phone number. CSBot replies with its number, public key, and a signature on the number. ARTBot verifies using that supplied key and caches the result. Explain how to poison the cached number as (i) an on-path attacker, (ii) a MITM attacker and (iii) an off-path attacker. Analyze a possible defense.
coverage_note: Cross-topic use of signatures, but the failure being examined is the absence of an authenticated public-key binding.

exact_skill: Leaked stack address and one-byte saved-frame-pointer overwrite

question: 2(c)
exact_skill: Off-path TCP injection and establishing a replacement connection
question_paraphrase: Using the printed TCP diagram (continued on p. 4), evaluate malicious actions by an off-path attacker and impersonating the client after it resets the connection.
